en: The Chapter on Similes, Section on the Monkey.

2. The Question on the One Quality to be Adopted from a Child at the Breast “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one quality should be adopted from a child at the breast,’ which is that one quality to be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, a child at the breast clings to its own purpose and cries out when seeking milk;”

In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga should fix his mind on his own true goal; he should possess knowledge of the Dhamma in all respects regarding recitation, inquiry, right application, seclusion, living with a teacher, and attending upon virtuous friends.
This, Great King, is one quality that should be adopted from a child who stays at home.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* of the excellent *Dīgha Nikāya*:
“Come now, Ānanda, strive for the essential, devote yourselves to the essential, and dwell diligent, ardent, and resolute regarding the essential.
This is the second question on the limb of one who has been established in the state.
